faq.q: Do email symbols work in Gmail and Outlook?
faq.a: Yes. These are standard Unicode characters, so they display in Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, and most modern clients on both desktop and mobile. Text-style glyphs (✆ ☎ ✉ ▸ •) are the most reliable; full-colour emoji also work but can render slightly differently between clients.

faq.q: How do I add an email or phone icon to my signature?
faq.a: Click the icon you want (✉ for email, ☎ or ✆ for phone, 🌐 for website, 📍 for address) to copy it, then paste it at the start of each line in your email signature. Text-style glyphs keep a clean, professional look and won't clash with your signature's font colour.

faq.q: Will symbols in a subject line send my email to spam?
faq.a: A single, relevant symbol is generally fine and can lift open rates. The spam risk comes from overuse: multiple flashy emoji, ALL CAPS, and spammy words together. Use one tasteful symbol that matches the message, and keep the rest of the subject line clean.

faq.q: What's the difference between an email symbol and an email emoji?
faq.a: Text symbols (✉ ☎ ▸ —) are monochrome glyphs that inherit your text colour and stay subtle, which suits professional signatures and bullets. Emoji (📧 📱 🔥) are full-colour pictographs that grab attention, which suits subject lines and casual reactions. This page includes both.
